# Known limitations and future work

<!-- Generated by scripts/build_docs.py from results/**/*.json. Edit docs/templates/limitations.md.j2. -->

## Statistical limitations, found by this repo's own validation

- **SRM has limited power against subtle, selective loss.** A 5% selective loss of treated users at n = 20,000 was flagged in only 59% of simulations, and a pre-period balance check (|SMD| > 0.05) in only 14%, while the estimate was biased (coverage 51%). A random 1% loss at n = 100k was flagged 4.3% of the time.
- **IPW under poor overlap** undercovers (76.9%) because its SE understates the variability (SE/SD = 0.59). Use AIPW, or trim and state the changed estimand.
- **IPW with bootstrap SE** covered 94.0% over 200 replications (100 bootstrap draws each). That is slightly under nominal and within Monte Carlo noise of 95%. More draws would be needed to say more.
- **IPW/AIPW on a binary outcome** covered 93.5% / 93.7% over 1000 replications (MC SE ≈ 0.7 pp): 1.5-1.3 pp under nominal.
- **The pre-trend test is weak.** A 0.03/period violation biased DiD by 0.147 and dropped coverage to 81%, but the test flagged it only 6.2% of the time. Honest-DiD style sensitivity bounds (Rambachan & Roth) would be the next step.
- **Uplift on rare binary outcomes needs a lot of data.** At 10k training rows the learners rarely produced a Qini CI excluding zero (8%) even with a real 0-vs-4pp split.
- **Newcombe CIs are conservative at very small counts** (97.2% coverage at n = 600, p = 1%). Wald was close to nominal there (94.9%) but undefined in 6 of 2000 samples.

## Scope limitations

- **DiD supports block adoption only** (one treatment date). Staggered adoption with heterogeneous effects biases two-way fixed effects (Goodman-Bacon 2021). Callaway-Sant'Anna or Sun-Abraham estimators are future work.
- **DiD has no real-data case study.** I found no suitable public panel with a genuine policy change and did not invent one.
- **The sequential design covers efficacy stopping only.** Futility bounds, unequal-information re-computation and always-valid (mSPRT) inference are not implemented.
- **CUPED uses a single covariate**, with theta estimated on the pooled sample. Lin regression handles several covariates. CUPAC (ML-predicted covariates) is not implemented.
- **Ratio metrics** (e.g. revenue per session with user randomization) need the delta method on the ratio. Only clustered means and relative lift are provided.
- **Uplift features in Criteo are anonymised**, so the targeting rule can't be explained or audited for fairness. The Criteo licence (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0) restricts use to non-commercial purposes.

## Case-study limitations

- **GA360 is observational, and purchase intent is unmeasured.** Cross-device journeys are invisible because cookies are per device. The suspected-internal segment (49% of desktop conversions) is identified by pattern, not confirmed. GA360 timestamps are UTC, so hour-of-day is not local time.
- **Hillstrom's profit decision** depends entirely on assumed margin and e-mail cost (`configs/hillstrom.yaml`).
- **Criteo uses a 7.2% seeded sample** for speed. The economic assumptions are illustrative, and the memo reports how the decision changes across them.

## Engineering notes

- On macOS with Apple Accelerate and NumPy 2.2 (the Python 3.10 lock), scikit-learn's logistic fit emits spurious `RuntimeWarning: overflow encountered in matmul`. All results are finite and the tests pass. The warnings are not suppressed.
- Full validation (`make validate`) takes roughly 15 minutes on a laptop. CI runs the quick versions only.
